analysis: All four units are documentation-only: docs/developer/test.md (head excerpts of existing test-lane text, plus an added 'Cluster Pair Coordinated Update' test section whose patch is truncated) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (a paragraph on `darkbloom update` asking the cluster service supervisor to restart the pair, and an auto_update table-row note). No executable code, configs, keys, endpoints, or authorization logic change, so no security regression is supported by the supplied evidence. No statement in the docs alters or claims a weakened control; they repeat that CPU tests grant nothing and do not qualify hardware. The cluster-prefix tenant partition docs and Qwen/GPT-OSS checks match the T-041 posture (tenant-scoped prefix keys, no cross-tenant reuse) without loosening it. The new described behavior, in which `darkbloom update` and the auto-update slot coordinate a restart of both cluster Macs after drain, introduces a pair-coordinated update path via the cluster service supervisor and a peer request. It touches the updater trust chain (T-013, T-043, T-061 adjacent: bundle/binary/metallib hash verification, rollback, start check of the candidate). The implementation (UpdateCommand.swift, ClusterServiceUpdateRequest, ClusterPairUpdateCycle) is not in the supplied batch, so peer authentication of the update/stop request, the replay or authority of that request, and whether a partner could trigger an update or denial of service on the other Mac cannot be assessed. Next pass should examine those sources, notably peer-authenticated control intent, and that the update path keeps the existing hash verification before install. The threat model may need a note on the pair-coordinated update boundary if the source adds peer-triggered restarts. The patch excerpt for test.md is truncated, so the full added section was not seen.
